text:
maria: Quick sync — launch aftermath: we have ~18 bugs and a few enhancement asks from Acme. I’m thinking a 2-week mini-cycle with ~60% bugfix focus, 40% enhancements. Thoughts?
jonathan: +1 on a focused mini-cycle, but we should triage by user journeys. Which issues are causing p99/regressions vs pre-existing tech debt?
kevin: I’ll sweep infra/latency flags today. Can someone mark regressions?
sophia: From CS: Acme called out the calendar export (blocking onboarding) and an embeddings mismatch. Export = high priority, bulk-embed-refresh = lower.
maria: Proposed routing: urgent queue (customer-facing hotpaths / sev2) -> 48h SLA, next bucket = two-week patch, rest -> backlog. Agree? :thinking_face:
jonathan: Sounds good. For the urgent queue I want a patch + feature-flagged canary path: patch -> canary -> full rollout if stable (48h window).
kevin: I can allocate 2 devs to urgent queue and +1 for monitoring. We should deprioritize one enhancement to free cycles.
sophia: Confirming Acme prefers export fix now. They explicitly asked we delay bulk embed work.
maria: Action items:
- jonathan: implement export patch + feature flag (EOD tomorrow)
- kevin: reserve 2 devs, set up canary and monitoring (48h)
- sophia: draft customer comms + CS playbook
- maria: move remaining enh to `next-wave` board and update roadmap notes
Also: I’ll add mini-cycle success metrics (time-to-fix, reopen rate, user-impact score).
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: release r2026.03.23-canary -> us-west (triggered by jonathan) :rocket:
jonathan: Quick check — logs look clean so far, p95 latency stable. I’ll post status at +6h and +24h.
kevin: Added labels `urgent-export`, `canary` to tickets. Ran `./scripts/assign -q urgent` — output: assigned 5 tickets to urgent queue.
maria: Thanks all. Reconvene tomorrow 10:00am PT to confirm rollout outcome. If anything spikes, ping #eng-oncall and I’ll reroute.
